39624.en: Theorem: X_39624 is the unique major center on the line at infinity.
no: Proof (by Shourya Pandey): First, suppose that \(f(A) : f(B) : f(C)\) is a major center on the line at infinity. Then f(A) + f(B) + \(f(C) = 0\). Define \(g(A) = f(A + \pi /3)\), or equivalently, g(A - π/3) = f(A). Let x = A - π//3, y = B - π/3, z = C - π/3, so that x,y,z are real variables such that \(x + y + z = 0\), and
Putting x = y = 0 in (*) gives \(g(0) = 0\), and putting y = -x in (*) shows that g is an odd function, so that
Equation (**) is the Cauchy functional equation, for which the only continuous solutions are \(g(x) = k x\). Thus, \(f(A) = k(A - \pi /3)\), so that
The method of proof shows that this solution is unique.
The domain of X_39624 consists of all non-equilateral triangles.

39641.en: The **real foci** of the Brocard inellipse are the Brocard points. They are a bicentric pair, with barycentrics 1/b^2 : 1/c^2 : 1/a^2 and 1/c^2 : 1/b^2 : 1/a^2, denoted by PU(1) in **Bicentric Pairs of Points** (``BicentricPairs.html``).
no: In contrast to the real foci, the **imaginary foci** of the Brocard inellipse are major triangle centers. They both lie on the Brocard axis, X_3X_6, and on the Kiepert circumhyperbola, and on the following curves: K003, K019, K049, K102, K115, K166, K248, K268, K326, K359, K369, K373, K444, K512, K516, K587, K588, K643, K688, K708, K731, K763, K801, K828, K833, K1096, K1098, K1103, K1113, K1139, Q019, Q039, Q065, Q073, Q088, Q094, Q138.
